messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High GPU memory pressure detected on pool gpu-svc-prod-eu-2. metric: gpu_mem_used_pct=96 -> 99% over last 60s. sample: CUDA_ALLOC_FAIL x 42 in 30s. Auto-pager: PagerDuty incident PD-98124 created -> https://pd.example/PD-98124 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Page fired to schedule 'eng-oncall' (policy: gpu-pressure). Primary: Alex. Escalation in 5m if unacked.

Alex (on-call): acked to @pagerduty. I'm on it. Initial triage: which pools, any recent deploys?

Dan: none in the last 30m. We're seeing kvcache evictions spike and a lot of CUDA_ALLOC_FAIL logs coming from runtime-gpu pods in eu-2. Probable fragmentation or runaway cache size. Metrics: kvcache_evictions/s went from 10 -> 120.

Maya: adding logs:
```
[2026-03-15T09:07:12Z] runtime-gpu-7f8c CUDA_ALLOC_FAIL: failed to allocate 1.2G
[2026-03-15T09:07:13Z] kvcache: evicted prefix=abc123 size=512MB
[2026-03-15T09:07:14Z] runtime-gpu-7f8c OOM: reserved=61GB avail=2GB
```

Alex (on-call): thanks. Is this isolated to a single node or all nodes in the pool?

Dan: looks across 6 nodes in pool. All showing similar memory high-water marks, but one node has significantly higher fragmentation. Could be long-lived model sessions eating GPU VRAM + kvcache growth.

Maya: mitigation options: 1) scale up pool (add nodes) 2) evict/clear kvcache on pods 3) restart runtime pods on the worst nodes 4) reroute traffic off eu-2 to eu-1 temporarily.

Alex (on-call): immediate plan: clear kvcache on affected pods to free VRAM, then if still high, restart runtime on the 3 worst nodes. Put temporary routing rule to shed new heavy jobs to eu-1. I'm going to run the kvcache clear command on the top offenders.

Alex (on-call): running:
```
kubectl -n production exec runtime-gpu-7f8c -- sh -c 'pkill -USR1 kv-cache || kvcachectl clear'
```

ops-bot: command queued on 3 pods: runtime-gpu-7f8c, runtime-gpu-9a1d, runtime-gpu-c3b4.

Alex (on-call): executed on all three. Immediate logs show fewer CUDA_ALLOC_FAIL errors but evictions still elevated. Pulled memory down ~6-8% on those pods.

Maya: good. Can you restart runtime on the most fragmented node as a next step? That tends to recover allocator fragmentation.

Alex (on-call): initiating restart on runtime-gpu-9a1d:
```
kubectl -n production rollout restart deployment/runtime-gpu --field-selector metadata.name=runtime-gpu-9a1d
```

ops-bot: rollout restart started -> pod restarted and came back in 28s. Node memory now reporting 72% used.

Dan: after restart, CUDA_ALLOC_FAIL count dropped to 2 in the last minute. kvcache_evictions/s down from 120 -> 30. Good signal.

Maya: still seeing sustained pressure on pool overall. Recommend temporary reroute: modify routing weight for eu-2 to 10% for heavy generation and route to eu-1/asia while we monitor.

Alex (on-call): applied traffic rule: eu-2 heavy generation weight -> 10%. Watch for customer latency.

pagerduty: PD-98124 acknowledged by Alex. Escalation hold canceled.

Dan: customer impact: two high-traffic customers (tenant-id: acme-inc, tenant-id: buildly) reported increased 5xx/retry rates and p95 latency jump from 420ms -> 2.3s in eu-2. We've rerouted new heavy requests so impact should stop growing; some in-flight jobs may still be affected.

Alex (on-call): posting short customer note to status channel after we confirm stability.

Maya: next steps: 1) follow-up postmortem ticket for kvcache growth/regression 2) add automated eviction throttle if evictions > 100/s 3) evaluate setting KVCACHE_MAX_BYTES to lower default for eu-2 4) consider minor bump to node count for eu-2 if seasonal load continues.

Priya (next-oncall): I'm standing by for handoff in 10m. Anything you want me to take over?

Alex (on-call): after 15m stabilizing, handoff to Priya. Summaries: cleared kvcache on top 3 pods, restarted worst pod, applied routing weight to 10%, monitoring metrics. Key alert PD-98124 acked. Customer impact mitigated but still watching 5xxs. Please continue to watch kvcache_evictions/s and CUDA_ALLOC_FAIL. I'll create follow-up ticket linking logs and actions.

Priya (next-oncall): ack. I'll take over. Watching dashboards and subscriber alerts.

ops-bot: PD-98124 status updated: resolved?no, monitoring. Linked ticket: RINF-3245 (investigate kvcache growth).

Alex (on-call): quick note for the postmortem: suspected regressions in recent runtime allocator patch from 2026-03-14 (commit cf3a2). Please keep that in scope.

Maya: copying commands used and snippets into RINF-3245. Also adding playback of evictions graph.

Priya (next-oncall): thanks, continuing watch. If evictions spike again, I'll trigger scaling + full pool rolling restart.

Alex (on-call): thanks team. Closing my active involvement, handing to Priya. :thumbsup:
